newsitem.title: USA: Big media companies settle with Web site in lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Big media companies settle with Web site in lawsuit.

text.p: The Washington Post Co. and five other media powers announced a settlement Thursday with TotalNews Inc. in their federal lawsuit over the way the tiny company's Web site provided links to their Web sites.

Under the settlement announced in a joint statement by the plaintiffs and defendants, the TotalNews Web site has permission to provide links to the plaintiffs' Web sites, but in such a way that Internet users will be taken directly to the media companies' sites.

Previously, TotalNews (http://totalnews.com) was set up in such a way that users who clicked on a link to a plaintiff's site would see that Web site, but wrapped in a "frame" containing advertising sold by Gilbert, Ariz.-based TotalNews and other TotalNews material.

In addition to the Post and its online subsidiary, Digital Inc., the plaintiffs were Time Warner Inc. units Time Inc., Cable News Network Inc. and Entertainment Weekly Inc.; Reuters Holdings Plc unit Reuters New Media Inc.; Dow Jones & Co. Inc., publisher of The Wall Street Journal and Barron's; and newspaper publisher Times Mirror Co.

Named as defendants in the lawsuit were TotalNews Inc. and the two companies that own it, Grouper Technologies Inc. and Datapix Inc., TotalNews President Roman Godzich and TotalNews employees Norman Bashkingy and Larry Pagni.
TotalNews launched the Web site Oct. 17, Godzich said in a telephone interview. The lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court Feb. 20. DJI.N
